messages:
Dev Patel: hey all — support enablement request for the guided onboarding checklist beta/GA. can we get a small set of macros/canned responses we can drop into tickets that point ppl to the new checklist + troubleshooting page? we’re seeing repeats of 401 (wrong key env), 429 (quota), streaming disconnects, CORS. would love 4–6 macros w/ links + the “if you don’t see the checklist” note (feature flag). aiming to have this ready before broader rollout.

Priya Shah: +1. from last 2 weeks triage, top patterns:
- 401: using prod key in test env / wrong org/project / key copied w/ whitespace
- 429: confusion between rate limit vs quota exhausted; ppl don’t know where to see usage dashboard
- streaming: disconnects in browser + proxies; need “retry/resume + keepalive” guidance
- CORS: calling API directly from browser; should proxy via backend
if we can standardize replies it’ll cut down back-and-forth a lot.

ZendeskBot: Reminder set by Dev Patel: “Support macros for onboarding checklist” due EOW.

Elliot Price: yep. docs side: the new troubleshooting page is in flight + will be the canonical destination for these. proposed stable URLs (these should be safe to share externally; we’ll keep redirects if we move IA):
- Troubleshooting: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/troubleshooting
- First production launch: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/first-production-launch
- Rate limits & quotas: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/rate-limits-and-quotas
- API keys: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/console/api-keys
if you need shortlinks, we can add go/ links internally but external should be the docs.* URLs.

Wei Chen: also adding anchors so macros can deep link to the right section (401 / 429 / streaming / CORS). not all are live yet, but planned anchors:
- …/troubleshooting#authentication-401
- …/troubleshooting#rate-limits-429
- …/troubleshooting#streaming-disconnects
- …/troubleshooting#cors-and-browser-requests
I’ll confirm final anchor strings once the PR merges.

Marissa Cole: re: “if you don’t see the checklist” — during beta it’s behind a feature flag + cohort targeting. support-facing guidance:
- some orgs will not see it yet
- if they are in cohort, checklist appears in Console home + in project overview
- we can offer links to docs regardless
I can provide a snippet for the macro that says “If you don’t see the checklist in Console yet, follow the same steps here…”

Dylan Brooks: also, for support workflows: we now have an admin override to reset checklist state (useful if it gets stuck / validation lag). not something customers can do yet.
if a ticket needs it, file an internal request w/ org_id + project_id and we can reset. we’re writing a runbook but tl;dr: it’s safe + doesn’t affect usage/billing.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: for the 401 macro, it’ll help to explicitly mention “test vs prod key” since we’re changing UI copy there. suggested checklist:
1) verify they’re using the key from the right project
2) ensure they didn’t mix test key in prod env (or vice versa)
3) confirm header is exactly `Authorization: Bearer <key>`
4) rotate key if it may be exposed
and remind them not to paste keys into tickets.

Dev Patel: awesome. I’m going to draft 5 macros based on this thread. quick sanity check on tone: we want them short, actionable, and to push to checklist + troubleshooting.

Priya Shah: + include 1–2 “what to send us if still stuck” fields (request id, timestamp, region) but NOT prompts/content.

Elliot Price: +1 on no prompt content. we should also link to “how to capture request id” doc snippet; if it doesn’t exist I can add a short section to troubleshooting.

Marissa Cole: here’s a suggested “no checklist visible” blurb:
“Guided Onboarding is rolling out gradually. If you don’t see the checklist in your Console yet, you can still follow the same steps in our docs here: <link>. If you *do* see the checklist, it will automatically update after you complete certain steps (first successful request, first streaming session, etc.).”

Dev Patel: draft macros below — please react w/ :thumbsup: if ok or reply w/ edits. (we’ll adapt to Zendesk macros but keeping copy here)

Dev Patel: **Macro 1 — 401 Unauthorized (API key / auth)**
“An HTTP 401 usually means the API key isn’t being recognized for this request.

Checklist:
1) Confirm you’re using an active key from the correct org/project in Console: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/console/api-keys
2) Make sure the header is `Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>` (no quotes).
3) Double-check you didn’t mix a test key vs prod key environment.

Troubleshooting steps + common pitfalls: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/troubleshooting#authentication-401

If it’s still failing, please share the request ID + approximate timestamp + region (don’t paste API keys or prompt content).”

Dev Patel: **Macro 2 — 429 Too Many Requests (rate limits / quota)**
“An HTTP 429 indicates you’re exceeding a limit (either short-term rate limit or account/project quota).

Start here:
- Rate limits & quotas overview: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/rate-limits-and-quotas
- Troubleshooting 429s: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/troubleshooting#rate-limits-429

Recommended fixes:
- Add retries with exponential backoff + jitter.
- Reduce concurrency / enable streaming if appropriate.
- Check usage + remaining quota in Console (Usage dashboard).

If you share a request ID + timestamp we can confirm which limit is triggering (no prompt content).”

Dev Patel: **Macro 3 — Streaming disconnects / incomplete responses**
“If you’re seeing streaming disconnects or truncated streams, it’s often due to network/proxy timeouts or client-side handling.

Common fixes:
- Ensure your HTTP client supports server-sent events/streaming and doesn’t buffer.
- Add retry logic for dropped connections.
- If behind a proxy, verify idle timeout/keepalive settings.

Troubleshooting guide: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/troubleshooting#streaming-disconnects

If you can share your SDK/language + request ID + timestamp, we can help isolate the failure mode (please don’t paste prompts).”

Dev Patel: **Macro 4 — CORS / calling from browser**
“If you’re calling the Hosted API directly from a browser, you may hit CORS restrictions. We recommend calling Redwood from a backend (server) and proxying requests from the client.

More details + examples: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/troubleshooting#cors-and-browser-requests”

Dev Patel: **Macro 5 — First production launch / production readiness**
“If you’re moving from a quick test to a production launch, we recommend following the ‘First production launch’ checklist (timeouts, retries, rate-limit handling, monitoring, and rollback guidance):
https://docs.redwoodinference.com/hosted-api/first-production-launch

Note: Guided Onboarding in Console is rolling out gradually. If you don’t see the checklist yet, the docs link above covers the same steps.”

Priya Shah: :thumbsup: on all 5. minor edit: in Macro 2, maybe add “check for bursts / batch requests” but otherwise looks great.

Elliot Price: :thumbsup: looks good. one note: I’ll confirm the final anchor IDs for troubleshooting once merged; if they change I’ll ping here. otherwise these are the right destinations.

Wei Chen: :thumbsup: I’ll make sure the anchor text matches exactly so Support doesn’t have to keep updating macros.

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: and I’ll add one internal-only note for Support: if user says “checklist stuck” (e.g., first request completed but step not updating), it may take a few mins. if >30 min, escalate + we can reset state.

Dev Patel: perfect. I’ll port these into Zendesk macros today and share screenshots in #support once live. thanks all.
